title: What longbook is and what it costs
body:
longbook remembers the payments that come back: rent, insurance, loan instalments, school fees, subscriptions, card fees and domain renewals. It keeps the next one in view on your iPhone and your Mac: in a Home Screen widget and in the Mac menu bar.

It also keeps the expenses you have already made, so you can see a month's spending in Reports.

## Where your records live

Everything is kept in a longbook folder in your own iCloud Drive, as a plain file you own. longbook doesn't connect to your bank. We never see inside your longbook.

## What it runs on

- iPhone with iOS 17 or later
- Mac with macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon

One purchase covers both, and both read the same folder, so a change on one shows on the other.

## What it costs

longbook is a one-time purchase, not a subscription. At launch:

- The first 100 buyers pay $38.
- The next 250 pay $98.
- Everyone after pays $149.

Prices in other countries are whatever the App Store, or the checkout on the website, shows there.

The purchase includes:

- the iPhone and Mac apps, and every update
- Family Sharing, so everyone in your Apple family gets longbook on their own account
- 12 months of longbook Cloud, free

## Trying it first

There is no trial. Instead you get a 7-day refund: within 7 days of buying, tap **Request a Refund** on the Account screen and Apple refunds you. If you bought on the website, write to Support or contact@longbook.app and we refund you through Polar. Before buying, you can look around a demo longbook filled with made-up data.

## longbook Cloud

Cloud is an optional add-on for the features that use our server, at $4 a month after the free 12 months. See "What longbook Cloud adds".

title: Getting started on iPhone and Mac
body:
## Install

Download longbook on your iPhone, your Mac, or both. The Mac app can also be downloaded from longbook.app, as the article "Buying longbook for Mac from the website" explains. One purchase covers every device signed in to your Apple Account, and your Apple family through Family Sharing.

## Your folder

longbook keeps your records in a longbook folder in your iCloud Drive, as plain files that you own and can back up. Apple syncs it, so your iPhone and Mac show the same longbook when they use the same iCloud account.

To keep it somewhere else, choose **Choose Folder** at setup. Syncing between devices comes from iCloud Drive.

## The first run

Setup has three steps: sign in, activate your longbook, then import a statement. Tap **Securely Upload Statement** to pick one, or **Skip** to start with an empty longbook. Once a statement is kept, your longbook opens.

## Add your first payments

You can fill your longbook in three ways:

- **By hand.** Add a payment with its name, amount and next due date.
- **From a bank statement.** Import a statement and longbook reads the charges for you. See "Import a bank statement".
- **With your AI.** Connect Claude or ChatGPT and ask it to find your bills and subscriptions. See "Connect Claude or ChatGPT".

Whatever is added for you waits on the **Proposals** screen until you keep it or undo it.

## Your answers at setup

Setup asks about the people you pay and the accounts you pay from. Your answers are kept as hints for reading your statements, not added to **People** or **Accounts**. To change them later, open **Optimize your data** in Settings.

## Settings on Mac

On Mac, Settings opens in its own window: choose **Settings…** from the **Settings** row at the foot of the sidebar, or press ⌘,. Its sidebar has **General**, **Appearance**, **AI**, **Statements**, **Data & Privacy** and **Tutorials**, with your longbook account at the top. **General** holds **About**, **Software Update**, **Home currency**, **Login Items and Menu Bar**, and **Help and Feedback**. **Software Update** has **Check automatically**. **Login Items and Menu Bar** has **Open at login**, **Show in the menu bar**, a **Keyboard shortcut** for the menu bar item, and **Hide the Dock icon**.

## Look around first

Not ready to add your own? Open **Try the demo** in Settings. It's filled with made-up payments so you can see how everything works, and it doesn't touch your own folder.

## Keeping the next payment in view

longbook doesn't send notifications. On iPhone, add the **next payment** widget to your Home Screen. On Mac, the next payment sits in the menu bar.

## Something not working?

Tap **Support** in the corner of any screen and tell it what you see; the camera button attaches a screenshot of your screen, which helps. To reach a person, tap **Ask a person** and Support opens an email to the team.

title: Import a bank statement
body:
longbook can read a bank or card statement and turn its lines into charges, so you don't type them in.

## How to import

1. On iPhone, open **Settings**, then **Import a statement**. It is also on the **Reports** screen.
2. Tap **Securely Upload Statement** and choose up to five files at once: PDF, CSV, plain text or Excel, scanned PDFs included.
3. If a PDF is locked, enter its password. The password stays on your device.
4. Review what was read. It is one list, drawn with the app's own cards: **Commitments**, then **Past expenses**, **People** and **Accounts**, every item ticked. Fix a name, a category or a person, or untick anything. Transfers between your own accounts, card bill payments, money in, and lines already in your longbook start unticked.
5. Tap **Add**, which counts the ticked items. The review closes, and what is recorded shows in **Proposals**, to keep or undo. Only **Add** or **Discard** closes the review.

Payments that repeat are offered as commitments, every one ticked. Every person the statement prints is offered under People, and every account it prints under Accounts: the statement's own account, named from its header even when no number is printed, and the accounts your transfers go to, your own among them. Untick what you don't want. You need to be signed in to longbook to import.

### Adding the people and accounts it finds

**Add accounts and people found in statements** decides whether the people and accounts start ticked. It's on unless you turn it off: on iPhone in **Settings** under **Import**, and on Mac in the Settings window under **Statements**, where it's called **Add accounts and people found**. With it off, they start unticked, and only what you tick is added.

## What is sent, and what is kept

To read a statement, longbook sends it a few pages at a time from your device to our server, and from there to Anthropic's Claude. If Claude can't answer, the same piece goes to OpenAI instead.

- Our server keeps neither the statement nor the charges read from it.
- We only record that an import happened, so we can count your monthly share.
- The pages carry whatever your bank printed, including any account number.

## How many you can import

Every account includes a monthly share of statement reading. longbook Cloud gives you a larger share.

## Use your own AI instead

**Use My Own AI** gives you a prompt for Claude or another AI, which reads the statement and writes into longbook. What it writes waits in **Proposals**.

## If a file is refused

longbook first checks that a file is a statement. A file that isn't, such as a receipt or a screenshot, is refused and nothing is read from it.

## If the charges look wrong

Undo the proposal on the Proposals screen and nothing stays in your longbook. Then in Support, tap **Ask a person** to open an email to the team, and tell us the bank's name and what went wrong. Please don't send the statement itself.

title: Connect Claude or ChatGPT
body:
Your AI can read your longbook and add to it: bills it finds in your email, subscriptions, receipts, anything you point it at.

## On a Mac, with Claude

In **AI Connections** (on Mac, the **AI** pane of the Settings window), tap **Set Up Claude Desktop**. Claude Desktop then reads your longbook folder directly, with no copy on our server.

## From any device, with Claude or ChatGPT

1. In Claude or ChatGPT, add a custom connector with this address: `https://longbook.app/mcp`
2. Sign in with your longbook account when asked.

First, in **AI Connections**, turn on **Let AI Read My longbook**. This uses longbook Cloud, because your AI reaches a copy of your longbook kept on our server. Turning it off deletes the copy at once. Your purchase includes 12 months of Cloud.

To let your AI add things, also turn on **Allow proposals**.

## Set it up with a prompt

At setup's statement step, **Use My Own AI** shows three steps:

1. **Enable** lets your AI read your longbook.
2. **Claude** or **ChatGPT** copies a prompt that adds longbook to that AI. In Claude it installs the longbook plugin, or adds the connector where plugins can't be installed. In ChatGPT it creates a plugin named longbook, with its website and icon. Paste it into your AI.
3. **Copy Prompt** copies the words that ask your AI to finish setting up your longbook.

## What your AI can do

Try asking:

- "Find subscriptions from my email"
- "Add my statement"
- "What do I pay next?"
- "What is coming in the next 30 days?"

Every change your AI makes waits on the **Proposals** screen with its name on it. Keep it or undo it with one tap. longbook also keeps your past versions, so you can go back.

## If it doesn't connect

- Check that you're signed in to the same longbook account in the app and in your AI.
- Remove the connector and add it again.
- Still stuck? In Support, tap **Ask a person** to open an email to the team, and tell us which AI you use and the message it shows.

title: Refunds, restoring a purchase and Family Sharing
body:
## Get a refund

Within 7 days of buying longbook, open the **Account** screen and tap **Request a Refund**. Apple handles the refund under its own terms. If the button doesn't show, ask Apple at reportaproblem.apple.com.

If you bought on the website, write to Support or contact@longbook.app within 7 days. We refund you through Polar, to the payment method you paid with. Receipts are in Polar's customer portal at polar.sh/ccs/portal.

A refund also ends the 12 months of longbook Cloud that came with the purchase, for you and for your family.

Refunds of Cloud's monthly fee are handled by Apple too. Cancelling Cloud stops the next renewal. It doesn't refund the current month.

## Restore your purchase

On a new device, or after reinstalling, open the **Account** screen and tap **Restore Purchase**. Use the same Apple Account you bought with.

Apple may ask you to sign in to your Apple Account, the one you use for the App Store. That sheet is Apple's, not longbook's: a longbook account signed in with Google or Apple has no password, and none is asked for here.

When the purchase is found, the screen says **Purchase restored**. When none is on that Apple Account, it says so, and you can sign out of the App Store and in with the account you bought with.

## Family Sharing

Your purchase covers everyone in your Apple family:

- Each person installs longbook on their own devices and uses their own longbook account.
- Each family member also gets the free 12 months of Cloud.
- Each person's longbook is their own folder in their own iCloud. Family members don't see each other's records unless you share a report.

If a family member doesn't see longbook as purchased, check that purchase sharing is on in your Apple family settings, then restore on their device.

## Charged twice?

In Support, tap **Ask a person** to open an email to the team, and tell us the date of each charge. Please don't send card numbers. Apple's receipt email is enough.

title: What longbook Cloud adds
body:
longbook works on its own with your iCloud. Cloud is an optional subscription for the few features that need our server.

## What you get

- **Your AI on any device.** Claude, ChatGPT and other AI apps reach your longbook from your phone or the web, through the longbook connector and access keys.
- **Shared reports.** Share a spending report with family as a link and a password. They can view it and comment from any browser.
- **More statement reading.** A larger monthly share of statements read for you.

Viewing a report someone shared with you needs no subscription.

## What it costs

- Your longbook purchase includes 12 months of Cloud, free, for you and your Apple family. A purchase on the website includes the 12 months too.
- After that, Cloud is $4 a month through the App Store, or your country's price.
- Cloud is bought and cancelled inside your Apple Account's subscription settings. Deleting the app doesn't cancel it.
- The website doesn't sell Cloud for months after the first 12.

## What it keeps

When you turn on the connector, a copy of your longbook is kept with your account so your AI can read it. It's encrypted, and you can turn it off at any time, which deletes the copy at once.

The copy is also deleted after 90 days without the app refreshing it, or 30 days after Cloud ends.

## Without Cloud

Everything else keeps working: your records, reminders, widgets, imports within the included share, and Claude on your Mac reading your folder directly.

title: Signing in and your account
body:
## Why there's an account

Your longbook account carries your licence and your Cloud subscription. It also connects your AI to longbook and holds the reports you share. Your records themselves stay in your own iCloud.

## Ways to sign in

- **Sign in with Apple**
- **Sign in with Google**
- **An emailed code.** Enter your email and we send you a code to enter.

## If the code doesn't arrive

- Check your spam or promotions folder.
- Wait a minute before asking for another. Each address can get only a few codes an hour, to stop misuse.
- Make sure the address is spelled right.

Still nothing? In Support, tap **Ask a person** to open an email to the team, and tell us the address you used.

## Signed in on a new device

When you sign in on a new device, we email you a notice. If it wasn't you, sign out of all sessions from the app's sign-out screen and tell us.

## Delete your account

Open the **Account** screen and tap **Delete Account…**, then confirm.

Deleting your account removes your email and everything hosted for you: the copy for your AI and your shared reports. It doesn't touch the longbook folder in your iCloud. Your records stay yours.

If you bought Cloud, cancel it in your Apple Account's subscription settings too. Deleting the account doesn't cancel it.

title: Your privacy in Support
body:
## We never see inside your longbook

Your records live in your own iCloud. Support never asks for them, and we can't open them.

## What to leave out of a message

Please don't paste or attach:

- account or card numbers, card details or PINs
- amounts, balances or statements
- passwords or sign-in codes

To show a problem, describe it, or attach a screenshot with the camera button. The screenshot goes with your message to the AI, which reads it to see your screen and never repeats what it shows. It may show amounts, so check it first.

## Who answers

longbook Support is an AI. It answers from these help articles, using Anthropic's Claude through longbook's server. When it doesn't know, or you'd rather ask a person, tap **Ask a person**: it opens your own email to contact@longbook.app with the conversation in it, and you send it yourself. Someone on the team replies to you by email.

## What Support keeps

- **On your device:** your conversation, so you can come back to it.
- **On our server:** nothing you wrote. We only count questions, note which articles answered them and how you rated them, and, when an article was missing, a short topic with no names or numbers, so we know what to write next.
- **In our inbox:** only an email you choose to send us.
- **At Anthropic:** your messages are used only to answer you, kept briefly under its commercial terms, and never used to train its models.

A screenshot you attach goes with that one message, to our server and to Anthropic, the same way as your words. Our server doesn't keep it. From the attachment you can send it to the team by email instead.

## Forget your conversation

In the app, tap **Clear support history** on the Help & about screen. To have an email deleted from our inbox, write to contact@longbook.app.

title: What each screen in longbook is for
body:
## On iPhone

The bottom bar has five places:

- **Dashboard**: the next payment, the month's spending and where it went.
- **Calendar**: every payment on its day.
- **Add**: a new commitment or expense.
- **Reports**: one report for every month that has a confirmed charge.
- **Settings**: everything else.

Settings opens everything else: **Proposals**, **Insights**, **Bookmarks**, **Accounts**, **People**, **Import a statement** and **Add accounts and people found in statements**, **Trips**, **AI Connections**, **Display & currency**, **Data & privacy**, **Optimize your data**, **Try the demo**, **Tips**, **Tutorials**, **Help & about**, **What’s new**, and your account at the top.

## On Mac

The sidebar lists them all:

- **Overview**: Dashboard, Reports, Calendar, Commitments, Insights, Proposals.
- **Payments**: Accounts, and under it your starred accounts.
- **People**: People, and under it your starred people.
- At the bottom: **Add commitment**, **Settings** and the bookmark icon. **Settings** opens a menu with **Settings…** (⌘,), **What’s New**, **Send Feedback…**, **Check for Updates…** and **Quit longbook**.

**Payments** and **People** fold away with a click on their name. Star an account or a person on its screen to keep it in the sidebar.

## What each one is

- **Commitments**: every payment ahead, grouped by month. **Past** lists every charge made.
- **Proposals**: what your AI, Siri or a statement import wrote, to keep or undo.
- **Insights**: short notes your AI left on your cards.
- **Accounts**: your banks, cards and wallets, each with its balance.
- **People**: who each payment is for.
- **Bookmarks**: the commitments you check most.

## Settings

On Mac, Settings is a window of its own, like the Mac's System Settings. Its sidebar has a search field, your longbook account, then **General**, **Appearance**, **AI**, **Statements**, **Data & Privacy** and **Tutorials**. Back and Forward (⌘[ and ⌘]) move between pages. **AI** is where you connect your AI, copy prompts, and set up Siri and Shortcuts; on iPhone that's **AI Connections**.

## Questions

### Where do I add a payment?
Tap **Add** on iPhone, or **Add commitment** in the Mac sidebar.

### Where do I see what my AI changed?
In **Proposals**.

title: Add a commitment or an expense
body:
A **commitment** is a payment that comes back: rent, a premium, an EMI, a subscription, a salary you pay. An **expense** is a payment you already made once. Both live in the same list.

## Add one by hand

Tap **Add** on iPhone, or **Add commitment** on Mac. The form asks for:

- a **name**
- **One-time** or a repeat: monthly, yearly or every few days
- the **amount**, with its currency
- the **first charge** and how far ahead to plan it
- a **category**, an **account** and a **person**, all optional
- **notes**

Extra fields sit under **More details** on Mac.

## Other ways in

- Import a bank statement.
- Let your AI find bills in your email.
- Ask Siri: "Add an expense in my longbook".

Everything an AI or Siri adds waits in **Proposals**.

## Keep it accurate

- **Mark paid** on a charge once it is paid.
- **Pause** a commitment, or set the day it stops.
- A new price applies to **Only This Charge** or to **This and Every One After**. Charges already paid keep their amount.
- Deleting a planned charge asks the same: **Only This Charge**, or **This and Every One After**, which also ends the commitment's plan there. Paid charges stay.

## Questions

### Does longbook cancel a subscription for me?
No. longbook records the cancellation: a commitment can be paused, cancelled or set to stop on a date, and its history stays. The cancelling happens with the provider.

### Can I add something that already happened?
Yes. Add it as **One-time** and mark it paid.

### Does longbook set a budget?
No. It records and totals what goes out.

title: Categories
body:
Every commitment can carry one category, and its charges take it. The dashboard, your monthly reports and your AI use categories to group spending the same way each month.

## What comes with longbook

Categories for subscriptions, streaming, rent, EMIs, insurance, salaries, utilities, education and more, each with its own icon. Any other category is added by name. A category is optional.

## Where you use them

- **Dashboard**: the **Categories** card totals the month by category with each one's share. Tap a tile to see that category's charges.
- **Reports**: each monthly report has the same breakdown.
- **All charges** and **Commitments**: filter by category.

## Rename or delete

**Edit Category** lists every commitment in a category, and a rename updates all of them. Press and hold a category in the commitment form, or right-click on Mac. A category you added can be deleted. Its commitments keep their money and lose the label.

## Questions

### Can a charge be in two categories?
No. A commitment carries one category and every charge takes it. Commitments without one are grouped under **No category**.

### How are statement lines categorised?
The import suggests a category for each line, from your categories and longbook's own, or leaves it empty. You can change any of them in the review before anything is added.

### Can my AI set categories?
Yes. Your AI reads the categories you use and sets one on what it adds. Ask it: "Categorise my longbook". It shows you the ones it guessed, and every change waits in **Proposals**.

### Can I tidy all my categories at once?
Ask your AI: "Reorganise my longbook". It gives every row a category and merges doubles. Amounts and dates are never touched.

title: People and accounts
body:
Each commitment can name one **person** it is for and one **account** it is paid from. Commitments can be filtered by both.

## People

A person is anyone a commitment is for: family, household help, a landlord, a tenant or a vendor. An optional relationship gives their role, such as Family, Cook or Landlord.

Each person has a card with their commitments, charges and accounts, and their next payment. **Add Commitment** opens the form with that person chosen. **Show All** lists their commitments. **Unassigned** holds commitments that name no one.

A person is a name in your records, not a sign-in. They don't need a longbook account.

## Stars, search and filters

Tap the **star** on a person or an account to keep it at the top of its list. On Mac, the sidebar lists only your starred people and accounts, under **People** and **Payments**.

Both screens have a search field. **People** filters by **Relationship**, and **Accounts** filters by **Type**: a menu on Mac, chips on iPhone.

## Accounts

An account is what pays a commitment: a bank account, a credit or debit card, UPI, a wallet or cash. Each account has one **Owner** (a person) or **Shared**.

Each account card shows its balance and date, its owner, the account it is linked to, and its next commitment with the total for the next 12 months. A card links to the bank account that pays it. Totals are per currency and count spending only.

longbook never stores a full card number. An account keeps at most the last four digits. The name printed on a card goes in the account's notes.

## Questions

### What happens if I delete a person or an account?
Their commitments stay, without that person or account. longbook tells you how many are affected before you delete.

### Does longbook connect to my bank?
No. Balances change only when you, a statement or your AI record one.

### Can a statement add people and accounts?
Yes, while **Add accounts and people found in statements** is on. It's on unless you turn it off: on iPhone in **Settings** under **Import**, and on Mac in the Settings window under **Statements**, as **Add accounts and people found**. The review then offers, ticked, every person the statement prints and every account: the statement's own account, and the accounts and people that transfers and card payments go to. Untick what you don't want before you tap **Add**. A closing balance on the statement updates its account.

With the switch off, they still appear in the review, unticked, and nothing is added unless you tick it.

### Are my answers from setup added as people and accounts?
No. **Optimize your data** keeps your answers, such as a cook or a card, as hints for reading your statements. They help your AI and the statement reader name things, but **People** and **Accounts** list only what you add or what a statement shows.

title: Currencies
body:
Every commitment keeps its own currency, and each currency is totalled on its own. longbook never converts one into another.

## Set a currency

The commitment form has a currency beside the amount. INR, USD, EUR and GBP are on the quick selector, and the **Currency** list adds any other, searchable by code or name.

## Totals

- The dashboard totals one currency and lists the others beside it. A menu at the top switches between them.
- **Commitments** and **All charges** can be filtered by currency.
- A monthly report totals one currency and lists every charge in its own.
- Your AI gets totals per currency, never converted.

## Home currency

On iPhone in **Settings**, under **Display & currency**, and on Mac in the Settings window under **General**, **Home currency** sets which currency the dashboard leads with. **Automatic** leads with the one most recurring commitments use. The choice appears once your recurring commitments use more than one currency.

## Questions

### Does longbook convert currencies?
No. longbook holds no exchange rates, so a total never moves with the market.

### Which currencies can I use?
Any currency in current use, by its three-letter code.

### What currency does Siri use?
An amount said in rupees, dollars, pounds, euros, dirhams or yen keeps that currency. Any other amount takes the currency most of your commitments use.

title: The dashboard
body:
The dashboard shows what is due next and what each month cost, by day, by account and by category.

## What is on it

- **Next payment**: days to the next payment, with its name and amount.
- **Commitments**: how many are active.
- **Coming up**: the next 30 charges and transfers in date order. The control at its left edge switches to past charges.
- **Spending**: the month's total, its number of charges and a bar for each day. For the current month it also shows the amount still to come.
- **Money in**: shown under the total, never added to it.
- **Accounts**: the month split by the account that paid, in a ring.
- **Categories**: the month split by category, with each share.

The month picker opens any month that holds charges. Tap an account or a category to see that month's charges for it.

## A new longbook

Until your longbook holds a commitment or a charge, the dashboard shows one card, **Start with a statement**, with three ways in: **Import a statement**, **Add a commitment by hand**, or **Use your own AI**, which opens **AI Connections** (on Mac, the **AI** pane of the Settings window). On Mac, you can also drop a statement file from Finder onto the card.

## Questions

### Does it include transfers?
No. Transfers between your own accounts, such as a card bill, are left out of spending.

### Does longbook set budgets or forecasts?
No. It reports the charges your records hold, past and planned.

### Does longbook write insights about my spending?
No. longbook draws the figures. When your AI leaves a note, it shows as a mark beside that card.

### How are several currencies shown?
One at a time, never converted. See "Currencies".

title: The calendar and bookmarks
body:
## The calendar

The **Calendar** shows every payment on its day, twelve months back and twelve ahead.

- Each day with a payment shows how many, with up to three dots in category colours.
- A transfer, such as a card bill, has its own mark and isn't counted.
- Step by month with the arrows or a swipe. **Today** returns to the current month.
- Tap a day to list its payments and transfers with their amounts. Each has **Mark Paid** from today on. **Show in Commitments** opens the full list for that day.

The calendar is drawn inside longbook. Nothing is written to Apple Calendar or Google Calendar, and money in is not shown on it.

## Bookmarks

A bookmark saves a commitment to one short list, so the ones you check most stay together.

- Swipe right on a row on iPhone, or right-click on Mac, and choose **Bookmark**.
- **Bookmarks** opens the list. It is in Settings on iPhone, and is the bookmark icon at the foot of the Mac sidebar.
- **Bookmarked Only** in the **Commitments** filters narrows the list to them.

A bookmark changes nothing about a commitment. It is a display setting saved in the longbook folder, so it shows on iPhone and Mac when both open the same folder. Your AI can't see bookmarks.

## Questions

### Does longbook remind me before a payment?
Yes. The next payment stays in view on the iPhone widget and in the Mac menu bar.

title: Monthly reports and sharing them
body:
## Reports

longbook draws a report for every month that holds a confirmed charge. It has the month's total, spending by account and by category, and every confirmed charge.

A charge is confirmed when a bank statement or an email proves it, you mark it paid, or you set its amount. A charge that was only planned doesn't count, and a month still to come has no report.

- **Not yet confirmed** counts the month's past charges nobody has confirmed, beside the total.
- Press and hold a charge for **Remove from report**. The charge stays in your longbook. **Put back** restores it.
- Transfers stay out of every report.
- Reports are in the home currency. Nothing is converted.
- Each report is a file in the reports folder of your longbook.

## Share a report

**Share report** makes a link and a password. The person opens the link in a browser, types the password, reads the report and comments on each section. They don't need longbook.

- The password is shown once. Send it separately from the link.
- The link expires after 3 days. **Stop sharing** ends it sooner and deletes the shared copy.
- **Pull comments** brings their comments into the report in your folder.
- They see only that one report.

## Questions

### I lost the password. What now?
longbook can't show it again. **Stop sharing**, then **Share report** for a new link and password.

### Can my AI make a report?
Yes. Ask: "Create a report in my longbook", or "Make a report of my Goa trip". It shows on the Reports screen.

title: Proposals: review what your AI writes
body:
Every row that an AI, Siri, a statement import or another program writes into longbook shows in **Proposals**, with its writer's name, to keep or undo.

## How it works

- Rows are listed in a tab for each kind: charges, commitments, accounts, people and categories.
- A changed row shows each field before and after.
- **Keep All** accepts the proposal. **Undo All** writes back the state from before it.
- Before you decide, you can edit or delete a row that was added.

## Not a queue

A proposal is already in your longbook when you see it, and the rest of the app counts it. **Keep All** confirms it. **Undo All** removes it, including anything edited since.

## History

**History** keeps the last 50 versions of your longbook, each with its writer, time and what it changed. **Restore** writes an earlier version back as one more proposal. It deletes nothing.

## Questions

### Can I keep one row and undo another?
No. **Keep All** and **Undo All** answer the whole proposal. Delete or edit a row first if you need to.

### What counts as a proposal?
Writes from an AI through the MCP server, Siri, the Shortcuts action, a statement import, or another program editing the file. Edits you make in the app's own forms don't wait for review. Notes your AI leaves on cards don't show here.

### Can my AI change things without my knowing?
No. Every proposal names its writer. Through the online connection, a signed-in AI can only make proposals, and only after **Allow proposals** is on.

title: Where your data lives and what leaves your device
body:
## Your longbook is a folder

Your records are plain JSON files in a folder called longbook in your own iCloud Drive. The main file is `financial_memory.json`. The folder also holds your monthly reports, your AI's insights and earlier versions. Apple syncs it to every iPhone and Mac on the same iCloud account. Any tool that reads JSON can open it. longbook never connects to a bank.

- **Move to iCloud** moves a folder kept on one device into iCloud Drive, and checks the copy first.
- **Back Up Now** makes a copy of the file to keep.
- You don't need iCloud. At setup, **Choose Folder** keeps longbook in a folder you pick. Syncing between devices comes from iCloud Drive.

## No card numbers

The format has no field for a full card number, a CVV, an expiry, a PIN or a password, and a save carrying one is refused.

## What can leave your device, only when you use it

- **Statements** you import go through longbook's server to Anthropic's Claude to be read. longbook keeps neither the file nor the charges.
- **Hosted copy**: a copy for online AI connectors, kept only while you have AI access on. Turning it off deletes it.
- **Shared reports**: kept until the link expires or you stop sharing.
- **Your account**: your email and licence status.
- **Usage and crash data**: counts, never a name, amount or note. Switch it off in Help & about.
- **Support**: questions you ask in Support go through longbook's server to Anthropic's Claude, which answers from these help articles. Our server doesn't keep them, and Anthropic keeps them only briefly and doesn't train on them.

longbook never sells your data. We never see inside your longbook.

## Questions

### What happens if I delete my account?
**Delete Account** removes your email and anything hosted. Your folder stays where it is.

title: The widget and the Mac menu bar
body:
Both keep your next payment in view without opening longbook.

## iPhone widget

A Home Screen widget called **next payment**, in small and medium sizes. To add it, press and hold the Home Screen, add a widget, and search for longbook.

- The day reads **Today**, **Tomorrow** or a count of days, with the total and each commitment due.
- Paused and cancelled commitments, charges marked paid, and money in are left out.
- Totals are per currency, never converted. A transfer, such as a card bill, shows on its own line.
- The medium size also names the person each payment is for.
- It reads your folder in iCloud Drive, and refreshes after midnight and when the app loads a change.
- If it can't read the folder it shows **open longbook**. Opening the app fixes it.

There is no Lock Screen widget.

## Mac menu bar

The longbook item in the menu bar shows the total due on the next payment day and how far away it is. The menu names each commitment due, lists transfers separately, and has **Open longbook**, **Refresh** and **Quit longbook**.

- It stays while the app is running, even with every window closed.
- In the Settings window, under **General**, then **Login Items and Menu Bar**: **Open at login** starts longbook when you log in, **Show in the menu bar** turns the item on or off, **Keyboard shortcut** opens it from any app, and **Hide the Dock icon** keeps longbook in the menu bar only.
- It re-reads the folder when the day changes, the Mac wakes, and each time the menu opens.

There is no widget for the Mac.

title: Siri and Shortcuts
body:
Siri adds payments to longbook by voice, and says what is due next. A Shortcuts action records charges from your bank's messages.

## Say it to Siri

- **"Add an expense in my longbook"** records a payment you already made.
- **"Add a commitment in my longbook"** adds a one-time payment due on a day.
- **"What do I pay next in my longbook"** names each payment due on the next day anything is owed, with its amount.

Siri asks for the name, the amount and the day. Rupees, dollars, pounds, euros, dirhams and yen keep their currency. Any other amount takes the currency most of your commitments use.

## Charges from bank messages

The **Record a charge from a message** action reads a bank message on your device: the amount, the day, the payee, and the account whose name holds the same last four digits. A credit is recorded as money in. One-time passwords, declined payments and balance alerts record nothing. The same message handed over twice records one charge.

The action reads only the text a shortcut gives it. To run it on its own, build an automation in the Shortcuts app with a Messages or Mail action.

## Questions

### Can Siri add a monthly or yearly commitment?
No. Siri adds a one-time commitment. Set a repeat in the commitment's form in the app.

### Where does Siri write?
To the longbook folder in iCloud Drive, without opening the app. iCloud Drive has to be on. Everything it adds shows in **Proposals** as Siri.

title: Connect your AI to longbook (MCP)
body:
Your AI reads your longbook and writes into it through longbook's MCP server. There are two ways to connect.

## Online, from any device

Needs **longbook Cloud** ($4 a month, the first 12 months included with your purchase). Your AI connects to:

`https://longbook.app/mcp`

- **Claude**: Settings, Connectors, **Add custom connector**, paste the address, sign in with your longbook account.
- **ChatGPT**: Settings, Connectors, add the address, sign in.
- **Claude Code**: `claude mcp add --transport http longbook https://longbook.app/mcp`, then run `/mcp` to sign in.
- **Other AI apps** that support remote MCP: point them at the address.

First, in **AI Connections** (on Mac, the **AI** pane of the Settings window), turn on **Let AI Read My longbook**. Your AI then reads a copy only your account can reach. To let it suggest changes, also turn on **Allow proposals**. Suggestions wait in **Proposals**.

## On your computer, free

No account and no hosted copy. See "Run longbook's server on your computer".

## Questions

### Which AI works?
Claude, ChatGPT, and any assistant that supports MCP connectors.

### Can my AI change things without asking?
No. It can only make proposals online, and every proposal shows in **Proposals** with its name.

### How do I disconnect an AI?
Disconnect it in **AI Connections**, or turn off **Let AI Read My longbook**. It takes effect at once, and turning it off deletes the copy.

### I'm stuck.
In Support, tap **Ask a person** to open an email to the team, and tell us which AI you use and the message it shows.

title: What your AI can do in longbook
body:
Once connected, your AI uses longbook's tools. Every number comes from the same engine the apps use, in each currency, never converted.

## It can read

- the next payment, and what is due soon
- cash flow over any dates
- your commitments and your charges
- spending by category, by account and by person
- your accounts, people and categories
- a search across everything
- the longbook guide, so it knows the format

On your computer it can also read the bank statements in your documents folder and the monthly reports longbook drew, with their comments.

## It can write

- add commitments and charges
- change a commitment, mark a charge paid, remove charges
- cancel a commitment
- leave a note on a card (see "Notes from your AI")

Every write is checked against longbook's format. It can't hold a card number, a CVV, an expiry, a PIN or a password. Writes land in **Proposals** with the AI's name, to keep or undo.

## Questions

### Can it see my bookmarks?
No. Bookmarks aren't part of what the server shares.

### Does it need my bank login?
No. longbook never connects to a bank, and your AI doesn't need one.

### What should I ask it?
See "Prompts to set up and keep longbook current" and "Prompts to ask, report and tidy".

title: Run longbook's server on your computer
body:
The longbook MCP server also runs on your own computer. It reads your longbook folder directly. It is free, needs no account, no hosted copy and no longbook Cloud, and works offline.

`npx -y @longbook/mcp@latest`

You need Node.js 18 or later. `npx` comes with it and fetches the newest release each time. You also need the longbook app, which creates the folder.

## Add it to your AI app

Add a server named **longbook** with the command `npx` and the arguments `-y` and `@longbook/mcp@latest`, then restart the app.

- **Claude Desktop** on Mac: **Set Up Claude Desktop** in the app does it in one click.
- **Claude Code**: `claude mcp add longbook -- npx -y @longbook/mcp@latest`
- **Cursor**: add it to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`.
- **VS Code**: `code --add-mcp '{"name":"longbook","command":"npx","args":["-y","@longbook/mcp@latest"]}'`
- **Codex CLI** and **Gemini CLI** take the same command in their settings files.

On a Mac it finds your folder in iCloud Drive by itself. On Windows or Linux, add `--vault` and the path to your longbook folder.

## Questions

### Is it open source?
Yes, GPL-3.0. longbook itself is a paid app. The server doesn't check for a licence, but buying longbook is what keeps it improving.

### When do I need Cloud instead?
For Claude on the web, the Claude phone app, or ChatGPT. They run on other computers and can only reach the hosted connector.

### Where do changes go?
Into your folder at once, and into **Proposals** with your AI's name.

title: Prompts to set up and keep longbook current
body:
Paste a prompt into Claude or ChatGPT with the longbook connector on. Each one has written steps your AI reads from longbook, so the same words give the same result. What it adds waits in **Proposals**.

## Setting up

- **"Read my 12-month bank statement and help me set up my longbook"**: fills longbook from your statements, sets each account's closing balance, and plans the payments that clearly repeat.
- **"Add my statement in my longbook"**: records every charge on a statement as paid, keeps money in apart, and updates the balance.
- **"Add September month report in my longbook"**: records the month's statements and confirms the charges they prove.
- **"Categorise my longbook"**: gives every commitment without a category one.

## Keeping it current

- **"Add email invoices in my longbook"**: this month's bank alerts, receipts, bills and money in from your mail, each recorded once. Needs a mail connector.
- **"Add document invoices in my longbook"**: invoices and receipts you attach or keep in the documents folder.
- **"Add a commitment in my longbook"**: a new commitment or a one-time expense, on the account and person you name.
- **A daily email round**: your AI reads your mail every morning at 6 and records what moved. See "Log expenses from Gmail".

## From your email

"Find subscriptions", "expenses", "invoices", "insurances", "purchases", "bills", "loans and EMIs", "travel bookings" or "money in from my email and add them in my longbook". They need a mail connector.

title: Prompts to ask, report and tidy
body:
Paste these into Claude or ChatGPT with the longbook connector on.

## Ask (nothing in longbook changes)

- **"What's my next commitment in my longbook"**: the next day you owe something, and what is due.
- **"What is coming in my longbook in the next 30 days?"**: everything due, by day, with the total per currency.
- **"What did I spend in July in my longbook?"**: what you spent, and what is not yet confirmed.
- **"What renews this year in my longbook?"**: your yearly, half-yearly and quarterly payments, in date order.
- **"Make my weekly longbook page"**: one page for the week.
- **"Set up a morning brief for my longbook"**: a short summary every morning. Needs scheduled tasks in your AI.

## Reports

- **"Create a report in my longbook"**: over the days, accounts, people and categories you choose. Counts confirmed charges only.
- **"Make a report of my Goa trip in my longbook"**: fills in as the trip's charges are confirmed.

## Tidy

- **"Tidy my longbook"**: finds doubled charges, bank-style names and odd categories, and fixes each one once you approve it.
- **"Reorganise my longbook"**: one pass over the whole book. Names as you'd say them, every row in a category, people and accounts linked, doubles merged, nothing lost. Amounts and dates are never touched. It waits in **Proposals** as one proposal.

In the app, **Reorganise my longbook** on the AI Connections screen runs it with longbook's own AI. It is limited each month, and more with Cloud.

title: Log expenses from Gmail every morning
body:
Claude can read your mail every morning and record what it finds in longbook. Each entry waits in **Proposals**.

## What it needs

- a longbook account with **Let AI Read My longbook** and **Allow proposals** turned on in **AI Connections**
- Claude with the longbook connector, a mail connector such as Gmail, and scheduled tasks

Without scheduled tasks, Claude can run the same round when you ask.

## Set it up

In the app, open **AI Connections**, find **Claude automation**, and tap **Copy Prompt**. Paste it into Claude. Claude schedules itself for 6am each day and runs the first round at once.

## What each round does

It reads the last day of mail for bank and card alerts, receipts, bills that are due, money in, renewal notices and card statements.

- A payment for a commitment longbook already holds becomes that commitment's charge.
- A card bill is recorded as a transfer, kept out of spending.
- One-time passwords, sign-in alerts and offers are skipped.
- Each entry keeps a reference to its email.

## Questions

### Does longbook read my email?
No. Claude reads it through its own mail connector and writes to longbook through the longbook connector. longbook never connects to a mailbox.

### Can the same payment be recorded twice?
The round checks what longbook already holds and skips an email whose amount and day are already recorded. Anything that slips through shows in **Proposals**, to undo.

title: Notes from your AI (Insights)
body:
Your AI can leave short notes on the cards they concern. longbook shows each note beside its card and gathers them all in **Insights**.

## How they look

A note sits on a dashboard card such as **Next payment**, **Spending** or **Categories**, or on the card of one account or one person. A speech-bubble mark beside the card's title opens it.

**Insights** lists every note by area: Dashboard, Accounts and People. The cross beside a note removes every note for that card.

## Where they come from

Only from an AI you connect, such as Claude or ChatGPT, through longbook's MCP server. longbook never writes a note itself. Notes are kept in a file called `insights.json` in your longbook folder.

## Questions

### Do notes wait in Proposals?
No. A note changes no commitment or charge, so it goes straight to its card. A note left through the online connection reaches its card the next time longbook is open and signed in.

### What if the AI has nothing to say?
Then no mark appears. A card shows the mark only when a note exists for it.

### How do I get a note?
Connect your AI and ask it a question about your month, an account or a person. Ask it to leave a note on the card.

title: What longbook does not do
body:
## It doesn't

- **connect to your bank.** Payments are typed in, read from a statement you pick, or added by your AI or Siri.
- **cancel a subscription.** It records the cancellation. The cancelling happens with the provider.
- **set budgets, targets or forecasts.** It records and totals what goes out.
- **convert currencies.** Each currency is totalled on its own.
- **write to Apple Calendar or Google Calendar.** The calendar is drawn inside longbook.
- **read your email itself.** Your AI reads it through its own connector.
- **keep your statements.** They are read and not kept. A copy of your longbook goes to our server only while **Let AI Read My longbook** is on.
- **offer a Lock Screen widget** or a Mac widget. The iPhone has a Home Screen widget and the Mac has a menu bar item.

## Coming later

- more devices: iPad, Apple Watch, iPhone Duo and Android, with the same licence
- **Income**: salary, interest and refunds in their own list
- **Available to spend**: what is left after everything already committed
- **Savings accounts**: your saved balance kept apart from spending

None of these is in the app yet.

## Questions

### Is there a free version?
longbook is a one-time purchase with a 7-day refund. Launch prices are $38 for the first 100 buyers, $98 for the next 250 and $149 after. The npm MCP server is free and open source (GPL-3.0).

### Can I ask for a feature?
Yes. Write to us in Support, or use the feedback board in Help & about.

title: Trips
body:
A trip gets its own report: what a holiday, a visit or a work trip cost, counted over its days, people and accounts.

## Start a trip

Open **Trips** (in Settings on iPhone, or ⌘7 on Mac) and choose **Start a trip**. longbook asks for:

- **Trip name**: what the trip's report is called, such as Goa or Mum's visit.
- **Trip people**: the people travelling.
- **Trip accounts**: the cards and accounts the trip is paid from. Choose none to count every account.

Tap **Start Trip**. **Trip mode** is on: the trip counts confirmed charges from today until you end it.

## Add a past trip

Choose **Add a past trip**, then give it a name, people, accounts and **Trip dates**: the first and last day. Confirmed charges on those days are counted. Tap **Add Trip**.

## End a trip

Tap **End Trip**. The report keeps the days from the trip's first day to today.

## See what a trip cost

**Trips** lists your past trips. **Open Report** opens a trip's report, which also appears in **Reports**. Like monthly reports, a trip counts confirmed charges only: ones a statement or an email proves, or that you marked paid.

## Questions

### Can my AI make a trip report?
Yes. Ask it: "Make a report of my Goa trip in my longbook". It fills in as the trip's charges are confirmed.

### Why is a charge missing from my trip?
It may not be confirmed yet, it may fall outside the trip's days, or it may be paid from an account the trip doesn't count.

title: Back up, export and delete your data
body:
## Your data is already yours

Your longbook is a folder of plain JSON files in your iCloud Drive, or in the folder you chose at setup. The main file is `financial_memory.json`. Monthly reports are files in the reports folder. Open the folder in Files on iPhone or Finder on Mac, and copy it wherever you like.

## Back up

In **Data & privacy**, tap **Back Up Now**. longbook makes a copy of the file exactly as stored, to share or keep.

**History** in **Proposals** also keeps your last 50 versions. **Restore** brings an earlier one back.

## Export to Excel or CSV

longbook has no Excel or CSV export. Two ways to get a table:

- Any tool that reads JSON can open `financial_memory.json`.
- Connect your AI and ask it to list your commitments or a month's charges as a table you can paste into a spreadsheet.

## Without a licence

If an account has no licence, everything stays visible and exportable. Nothing new can be added.

## Delete your longbook

**Delete longbook…** in **Data & privacy** explains how: delete the longbook folder in Files or Finder, like any other folder.

## Delete your account

**Delete Account…** on the Account screen removes your email and everything hosted for you: the copy for your AI and your shared reports. It doesn't delete your folder. If you have longbook Cloud, cancel it in your Apple Account's subscription settings too.

title: Mac keyboard shortcuts
body:
## Go to a screen

| Shortcut | Screen |
|---|---|
| ⌘1 | Dashboard |
| ⌘2 | Reports |
| ⌘3 | Calendar |
| ⌘4 | Commitments |
| ⌘5 | Insights |
| ⌘6 | Proposals |
| ⌘7 | Trips |
| ⌘[ | Back |

## Do something

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘N | New Commitment |
| ⌘I | Import Statement… |
| ⌘, | Settings… |
| ⌘? | longbook Help |

## In the Settings window

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| ⌘[ | Back |
| ⌘] | Forward |

In sheets and forms, Return confirms and Escape cancels.

## In the menu bar

The longbook menu also has **Check for Updates…** and **Tips**. The **Settings** row at the foot of the sidebar opens a menu with **Settings…**, **What’s New**, **Send Feedback…**, **Check for Updates…** and **Quit longbook**.

The longbook item in the Mac menu bar shows your next payment. Its menu has **Open longbook**, **Refresh** and **Quit longbook**. See "The widget and the Mac menu bar".

title: Troubleshooting and common questions
body:
### My iPhone and Mac show different payments
Both need the same iCloud account, with the longbook folder in iCloud Drive. A folder chosen elsewhere at setup doesn't sync. After a change, give iCloud a moment to sync.

### The widget says "open longbook"
It couldn't read the folder. Open the app once, and the widget shows the next payment again.

### The menu bar says "from the last copy"
iCloud is still downloading the folder, so longbook shows the copy it kept last time. Choose **Refresh** in the menu.

### My sign-in code didn't arrive
Check spam, wait a minute, and check the address. Each address gets only a few codes an hour.

### My statement was refused
longbook only reads statements. A receipt or a screenshot is refused. You can also use **Use My Own AI**.

### The import or my AI added something wrong
In **Proposals**, tap **Undo All**. To go further back, open **History** and **Restore** an earlier version.

### My AI can't reach longbook
In **AI Connections**, check **Let AI Read My longbook** is on, and sign in to the same longbook account in your AI. Online connections need longbook Cloud.

### Siri can't add to longbook
Siri writes to the longbook folder in iCloud Drive, so iCloud Drive must be on and the folder must live there.

### Does longbook send notifications?
No. The next payment stays in view in the iPhone widget and the Mac menu bar.

### Can my partner see my payments?
Family Sharing gives each person longbook with their own folder. To show someone your month, share a monthly report: they open a link with a password, no app needed.

### Still stuck?
In Support, tap **Ask a person** to open an email to the team, or write to contact@longbook.app.

title: Glossary
body:
**Commitment**: a payment that comes back, such as rent, a premium or a subscription. It can also be one-time.

**Charge**: one payment of a commitment, on one day, with its own amount.

**Expense**: a one-time payment you already made.

**Money in**: salary, refunds, interest and other money received. Shown under the total, never added to spending.

**Transfer**: money moving between your own accounts, such as paying a card bill. Kept out of spending.

**Confirmed charge**: proven by a statement or an email, marked paid, or given its amount. Reports count only these.

**Planned charge**: a charge longbook expects in the future.

**Person**: who a commitment is for. Not a login.

**Account**: what pays a commitment: a bank account, card, UPI, wallet or cash.

**Home currency**: the currency the dashboard leads with. Currencies are never converted.

**Proposals**: where everything written by an AI, Siri or an import waits, to keep or undo. Each batch waiting there is a **proposal**.

**Insight**: a short note your AI leaves on a card.

**Report**: one page for a month or a trip, built from confirmed charges.

**Trip**: a report over a trip's days, people and accounts.

**longbook folder**: the folder of plain files that holds your longbook, usually in iCloud Drive.

**longbook Cloud**: the optional subscription for features that use our server.

**MCP**: the connection your AI uses to read and write your longbook.

**Hosted copy**: the copy of your longbook kept for online AI, only while **Let AI Read My longbook** is on.

title: Buying longbook for Mac from the website
body:
You can download longbook for Mac from longbook.app and buy it there. The licence is the same one you get from the App Store: it covers every longbook app on your account, so it works on your iPhone too.

## Download

On longbook.app, open the Download page and choose **Download for Mac**. It is a notarised disk image for macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. Drag longbook to your Applications folder and open it.

## Buy inside the app

1. Open longbook for Mac and sign in to your longbook account.
2. Choose **Buy**. Checkout opens in your browser.
3. Pay there. Polar Software Inc. is the merchant of record: it takes the payment and handles the tax.
4. Return to longbook. The licence is on your account.

The licence lands on your longbook account, so signing in on your iPhone shows it there too.

## If you paid with a different email

The licence goes to the account with the email you used at checkout. If that isn't the email you sign in to longbook with, open longbook for Mac, choose **I have a licence key** and enter the key from Polar's email.

## Receipts and licence keys

Your receipts and licence keys are in Polar's customer portal at polar.sh/ccs/portal. Sign in there with the email you paid with.

## Refunds

Within 7 days of buying, for any reason, write to Support or contact@longbook.app and we refund you through Polar. The refund ends the licence and the 12 months of Cloud that came with it.

## Updates

longbook for Mac downloaded from the website updates itself from longbook.app. Every update is included in your licence.

## Cloud

A purchase on the website includes 12 months of longbook Cloud. The website doesn't sell Cloud for later months.
